Tabulation
Frequency table

Counts and percentages for each option. Choosing “Test whether responses are uneven” adds a chi-square goodness-of-fit test (chisq.test). For multiple-choice questions, the percentage of respondents choosing each option (the total exceeds 100%).
Frequencies of multiple questions

Tabulates questions with the same options side by side. For ordinal responses, the Friedman test (friedman.test; only respondents who answered all questions) and the effect size Kendall's W can be selected.
Numeric summary and histogram
n, mean, SD, minimum, quartiles, median and maximum. Bins can be automatic (one per value for integers with a narrow range), Sturges' formula or the Freedman–Diaconis rule.
Response timeline
Counts response date-times by day, week or month, with cumulative percentages.
Association between two questions
Chi-square test

chisq.test (no correction by default, even for 2×2 tables; Yates' correction is optional). Effect size: Cramér's V (φ for 2×2). Cells that are higher or lower than expected are identified by adjusted standardized residuals.
Fisher's exact test

fisher.test. For 2×2 tables, the conditional maximum likelihood odds ratio and its 95% CI. When the table is too large for exact calculation, it switches automatically to a Monte Carlo estimate (200,000 replicates).
Trend test for proportions
prop.trend.test (Cochran–Armitage). Levels are given equally spaced scores.
Stratified cross-tabulation

mantelhaen.test (no continuity correction; the generalized CMH test for tables larger than 2×2). chisq.test by stratum. For 2×2 tables, the common odds ratio (Mantel–Haenszel) with its 95% CI, and the Breslow–Day test (Tarone's correction).
Comparing ordinal responses
Mann–Whitney U test
wilcox.test (normal approximation with corrections for ties and continuity). Effect size r = |Z| / √N.
Kruskal–Wallis test
kruskal.test. Effect size ε² = H / (N − 1). Multiple comparisons with pairwise.wilcox.test (Holm method).
Spearman's rank correlation
cor.test(method = "spearman").
Comparing means
t-test
Welch's t-test (t.test). Student's t-test, which assumes equal variances, can also be selected. Effect size: Hedges' g. 95% CI of the mean difference.
One-way ANOVA
Welch's ANOVA (oneway.test) with Games–Howell multiple comparisons. Standard ANOVA assuming equal variances (Tukey method, TukeyHSD) can also be selected. Effect size: η².
Paired t-test
t.test(paired = TRUE). Effect size: dz (mean difference ÷ SD of the differences). 95% CI of the difference.
Two responses from the same people
Wilcoxon signed-rank test
wilcox.test(paired = TRUE).
McNemar's test
mcnemar.test (with continuity correction). binom.test (exact binomial test) when there are fewer than 25 discordant pairs.
Association and correlation
Pearson's correlation coefficient
cor.test(method = "pearson"). The 95% CI uses Fisher's z transformation. A regression line (lm) is drawn on the scatter plot.
Regression analysis
Multiple regression analysis

lm (forced entry). Partial regression coefficients B, SE, standardized coefficients β, 95% CI, t, p and VIF. R², adjusted R² and F test. Single-choice variables are dummy-coded with the first option as the reference; ordinal responses use level scores.
Logistic regression analysis

glm(family = binomial). B, SE, Wald test, odds ratios with Wald 95% CIs, and VIF. Likelihood-ratio test, Cox–Snell and Nagelkerke R², AIC, and classification accuracy (predicted probability cut-off 0.5).
Multiple-choice cross-tabulation
chisq.test or fisher.test for each option, adjusted with p.adjust (Holm method).
Scales and multivariate
Scale reliability

Cronbach's α and standardized α, ω coefficient (from the loadings of a one-factor factanal). Item means and SDs, ceiling and floor effects (whether mean ± SD exceeds the score range), item–rest correlations, and α if the item is deleted. Reverse-scored items are reversed before calculation.
Confirmatory factor analysis

Maximum likelihood (estimated with base R optim; factor variances fixed at 1 and factor correlations estimated). χ² test, CFI, TLI, RMSEA with 90% CI, SRMR, standardized loadings, SEs (from the Hessian), and ω (composite reliability) and AVE for each factor. Level scores are treated as numeric.
Exploratory factor analysis
Maximum likelihood (factanal). Promax rotation (with factor correlations) or varimax. With “Automatic”, the number of factors is the number of eigenvalues above 1 (Kaiser criterion).
Correspondence analysis

Singular value decomposition of the matrix of standardized residuals. Rows and columns are both shown in principal coordinates (symmetric map). The presence of an association is shown by the chi-square test.
Free text
Text mining

Splits text into words with the browser's word segmentation (Intl.Segmenter), joins consecutive kanji and katakana words, and removes function words. Frequent words, and a co-occurrence network based on Jaccard coefficients (Fruchterman–Reingold layout, label propagation for groups). When a group is selected, a chi-square test is performed for each word, with Holm adjustment.

<li>Loaded data and results are handled only
on this device

and are never sent anywhere. The app is not connected to any AI service.

• When loading from a Google Sheets URL, the app only receives the responses from that spreadsheet and sends nothing. To load it, the spreadsheet must be shared with “Anyone with the link” or published to the web.

• Excel files (.xlsx) are loaded by converting the first sheet into a table in the same form as a CSV. Dates become text in the form “year/month/day hour:minute:second”. The converted table (CSV) is stored in the project.

Analyses and calculation methods
R functions used and output
Rules common to all analyses
• For ordinal responses, the first option is treated as the highest when assigning ranks and scores.

• Respondents with no answer, or who chose an unchecked option, are excluded from that analysis. Numeric responses are used after correcting full-width digits, units and ranges (such as “1–2 hours”); responses that cannot be converted to numbers are excluded.

• The p value is the probability of a deviation at least as large as the one observed, assuming there is no association (no difference). A non-significant result does not prove that there is no association.
• The report also shows p values adjusted together with the Holm method for the tests marked with ☑ (can be switched in the settings).
• The lines in the “Mean and CI” figure are 95% confidence intervals of the mean based on the t distribution.

• A scale score (“Create scale score” under Data) is the mean or total of the scores of the selected items (reverse-scored items reversed). Scores are given only to respondents who answered all items. How it was created is written in the “Methods” of the analyses that use it.
Reproduction in Excel

The Excel file contains the data and cells in which the calculations are written with Excel functions. Results are not pasted as values; everything is a formula, so you can check how the values are calculated. The following cannot be obtained with Excel functions and are not included; use the app's values.
• p of Fisher's exact test for tables larger than 2×2
• p of multiple comparisons after ANOVA (Excel has no function for the studentized range distribution; the mean differences and t are included)
• Exploratory factor analysis (iterative computation)
• Dimensions and coordinates of the correspondence analysis (singular value decomposition; the chi-square test of association is included)
• Text mining (word segmentation)

• The generalized CMH test (tables larger than 2×2) of stratified cross-tabulation, and the CI of the common odds ratio and the Breslow–Day test (the chi-square tests by stratum, and the CMH test and common odds ratio for 2×2 tables are included)
• The ω coefficient of scale reliability, and confirmatory factor analysis (iterative computation)
• Logistic regression analysis (the coefficients require iterative computation; multiple regression is reproduced with the inverse of X'X)
p values of Welch's tests with fractional degrees of freedom are calculated with BETA.DIST, because Excel's T.DIST and F.DIST truncate fractional degrees of freedom.
Verification with R code

“Export” → “R code” saves a script (analysis.R) that recalculates the analyses marked with ☑ with standard R functions (chisq.test, t.test, lm, etc.), together with its data (analysis_data.csv). How options are combined, filters and scale scores are also written as code in the script. For numeric columns, the values corrected by the app (such as “40 min” → 40) are added to the data. When run, “>> App values” is printed after each analysis's results. Text mining and the response timeline use the app's own processing and are not converted to code. Confirmatory factor analysis is recalculated with the lavaan package if it is installed.

Citing in papers

Because this app is not widely distributed general software, in APA style and similar you should state in the text that you used it and its version, and also list it in the references. It is also common to cite R, which performed the calculations. If the journal or institution has its own rules, follow them.
